take_homes: Split agents only on access, dialect or stance. Before that, ask whether one good prompt does the job.

Put a framework such as Rumelt's kernel in the synthesizer so it picks one answer instead of averaging. The handoffs between agents are where the failures happen: a curator silently dropping a conflict between two sources.
A clean handoff audit doesn't mean the briefing is true, and nothing in this module checks that.

monday.move: Add a conflict-flagging rule to the synthesizer step of my sales-team setup so contradictions between sources are shown instead of dropped, and ask my team to spot-check one briefing against the sources
monday.who: me, plus one engineer to do the spot-check
monday.when: Monday morning, before I extend the setup any further
monday.stop_condition: the spot-check finds a briefing claim that no source supports; I stop adding agents until that is fixed
monday.blocker: Nobody in sales asked for the setup and nobody is named as maintainer; the spot-check is also the step I'd normally skip

misconception.why: The audit only checks how the agents handed work to each other, not whether the briefing is true, and the exercise output looked good. So good-looking output and true output can differ. I'm not fully convinced checking matters for my engineers, but I'd check the sales setup.

one_line: Good on when to split and where handoffs break. The first half repeats what my engineers already know, and the best part is the point that a clean-looking briefing can still be wrong.
